t: The Mamluk Sultanate was ruled from Cairo by slave soldiers, renewed by fresh purchases rather than hereditary succession.
It halted the Mongols at Ain Jalut, ended the Crusader states and grew rich on the spice trade between India and Europe.
Plague, Portuguese competition at sea and Ottoman guns brought it down, ending with Selim I's conquest of Egypt in 1517.
dyk: Though rulers of slave origin, the Mamluk sultans hosted a line of Abbasid caliphs in Cairo from 1261, whose nominal blessing lent them religious legitimacy.
ev: Mamluks assassinate Turanshah, the last Ayyubid sultan of Egypt, and seize power
Qutuz and Baybars defeat the Mongols at Ain Jalut; Baybars then takes the throne
Al-Ashraf Khalil captures Acre, ending the Crusader states
Al-Nasir Muhammad orders the rawk, a new land survey that reshapes the iqta system
The Black Death reaches Egypt, beginning repeated catastrophic population losses
Barquq inaugurates the Burji regime of Circassian mamluks
The Portuguese defeat a Mamluk fleet at Diu, cutting customs revenue
Selim I wins at Ridaniya and conquers Egypt, ending Mamluk sovereignty
